metadata.title: Long-Run SSP Population and Human-Capital Projections, 2025-Rebased, 2100-2300 (zen2300y2025V01)
metadata.description:
This dataset (version zen2300y2025V01) extends the 2025-rebased SSP population and human-capital projections beyond the conventional 2100 horizon to the year 2300. It is the long-run continuation of the 2025-2100 release (doi 10.5281/zenodo.21738149) and covers four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways: SSP1, SSP2, SSP3, and SSP5. Results are disaggregated by region, sex, five-year age group, and six levels of educational attainment, at five-year intervals, for 200 countries and territories together with UN area, subregion, and world aggregates. Files are gzip-compressed CSV and can be read without unpacking. 

Each scenario is provided as a separate file. The dataset also includes a recode dictionary, a file overview, and a README describing structure and caveats.

No SSP4 extension. The long-run extension was produced for SSP1, SSP2, SSP3, and SSP5 only. Analyses requiring SSP4 must stop at 2100.

metadata.method:
These projections are produced with the Multidimensional Demographic Modelling (MDM) workflow, the multidimensional cohort-component model used for the Wittgenstein Centre (WIC) population and human-capital projections (Lutz, Butz & KC, 2014; KC & Lutz, 2017). Population is projected in five-year steps by country, sex, five-year age group, and six levels of educational attainment (no education, some primary, primary, lower secondary, upper secondary, post-secondary).

The projections to 2100 build on the WIC2023 round of the SSP population and human-capital projections (KC et al., 2024), re-anchored on the projected 2025 population by age, sex, and education from the SSP2 pathway. That 2025 state is the common jump-off for all pathways, with the SSP1, SSP3, and SSP5 assumptions (O'Neill et al., 2017) applied from 2025 onward. SSP2 is unchanged by the re-basing: the SSP2 pathway already passes through its own 2025 state, so the re-based SSP2 and the original SSP2 describe the same trajectory, and the SSP2 file here is identical to the corresponding file in the 2020-based long-run record.

Long-run assumptions. Beyond 2100 the pathways converge to fixed fertility and mortality schedules. The SSP2 total fertility rate converges to 1.75 children per woman by 2200 across all countries. For SSP1 and SSP5, the low-fertility variant applied to the education-specific fertility schedules yields a global average near 1.53 by 2200; for SSP3, the high-fertility variant yields approximately 1.97. These last two values are outcomes of the variant schedules and the population composition, not independently imposed global convergence targets in the way the SSP2 value is. Life expectancy at birth is assumed to continue rising toward a cap of 105 years for both sexes; some countries do not reach that level by 2300. Net international migration converges toward zero in the long run.

Horizon. The SSP1, SSP3, and SSP5 source runs extend to 2500, but all four scenarios are truncated here at 2300 so that the set is internally uniform and directly comparable with the 2020-based long-run record.

Relationship to other releases 

Wittgenstein Centre (WIC) Population and Human Capital Projections 2023, V14, 2020 base to 2100: doi 10.5281/zenodo.14718294. SSP Projections, 2025-rebased, 2025-2100: doi 10.5281/zenodo.21738149, which this dataset continues in time. SSP Population Projections to 2300 (zen2300V15), 2020 base, 2100-2300: doi 10.5281/zenodo.18596542, which covers the same years from a different base year. Re-basing changes long-run totals by under one percent and leaves SSP2 identical, but the two long-run records should not be mixed within a single analysis.

Notes for users

The files contain individual countries together with UN area, subregion, and world aggregates in the same table. Filter on the region_level column before aggregating, otherwise totals will be double-counted. Rows with agest = -5 are a newborn accounting placeholder rather than a stock age group and should be excluded when computing population stocks; a small number of terminal-period rows at that age carry negligible negative values as a rounding artefact.

These are scenario outputs, not probabilistic forecasts. Two centuries beyond the conventional projection horizon, they are best read as a disciplined thought experiment about what follows if the demographic assumptions embedded in the SSPs are maintained, not as predictions. Country-level results for small territories warrant particular caution; in this version Mayotte shows implausible long-run growth arising from its high starting fertility combined with a small  opulation denominator.

metadata.title: SSP Population and Human-Capital Projections, 2025-Rebased, 2025-2100 (zen2025V01)
metadata.description:
This dataset (version zen2025V01) provides population and human-capital projection
outputs for the five Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), re-based on a 2025 jump-off
population, covering 2025-2100 at five-year intervals. Results are generated with the
Multidimensional Demographic Modelling (MDM) workflow, the cohort-component machinery
used for the Wittgenstein Centre / SSP projections, and are disaggregated by region, sex,
five-year age group, and six levels of educational attainment. All files are provided in
open CSV format.

Each scenario is uploaded as a separate CSV file, allowing users to download only the
pathway they need. In addition to the projection outputs, the dataset includes a recode
dictionary and a file overview to support interpretation, together with a README
describing the structure and known caveats.

The projection files contain five-year interval estimates of population size, births,
deaths, immigration, and emigration by region, sex, age, and education. Variable
descriptions, value labels, and category mappings are provided in Recode dictionary.csv.

Note on SSP2: SSP2 is unchanged by the 2025 re-basing. The re-basing takes the SSP2
projection's 2025 population as the new jump-off state and applies the SSP1, SSP3, SSP4,
and SSP5 assumptions from 2025 onward. SSP2 projected from the earlier base year already
passes through exactly that state, so the 2025-based SSP2 and the original SSP2 describe
the same trajectory. All five scenarios therefore share an identical 2025 population of
approximately 8.15 billion, and the SSP2 file serves as the common reference pathway.

Notes for users: the files contain individual countries together with UN area, subregion,
and world aggregates in the same table. Filter on the region_level column before
aggregating, otherwise totals will be double-counted. Rows with agest = -5 are a newborn
accounting placeholder rather than a stock age group and should be excluded when computing
population stocks; a small number of terminal-period rows at that age carry negligible
negative values as a rounding artefact.

These are scenario outputs, not probabilistic forecasts. They should not be read as
predictions, and long-run country-level results for small territories warrant particular
caution.

metadata.method:
These projections are produced with the Multidimensional Demographic Modelling (MDM)
workflow, the multidimensional cohort-component model used for the Wittgenstein Centre
(WIC) population and human-capital projections (Lutz, Butz & KC, 2014; KC & Lutz, 2017).
Population is projected in five-year steps by country, sex, five-year age group, and six
levels of educational attainment (no education, some primary, primary, lower secondary,
upper secondary, post-secondary). Coverage is 200 countries and territories; UN area,
subregion, and world figures are aggregated from the country results.

Starting point. The scenarios build on the WIC2023 round of the SSP population and
human-capital projections (KC et al., 2024). WIC2023 uses 2020 as its reference year and
revised the treatment of fertility, mortality, education, and migration relative to earlier
rounds, including updated education-specific fertility estimates, country- and
region-specific education differentials in mortality, and, for the first time,
education-specific migration rates.

The 2025 re-basing. Rather than re-estimating a new empirical base year, the scenarios in
this dataset are re-anchored on the projected 2025 population by age, sex, and education
from the SSP2 pathway. That 2025 state becomes the common jump-off for all five SSPs, and
the SSP1, SSP3, SSP4, and SSP5 assumptions (O'Neill et al., 2017) on fertility, mortality,
educational attainment, and migration are applied from 2025 onward.

One consequence deserves emphasis: SSP2 is unchanged by the re-basing. The SSP2 pathway
projected from 2020 already passes through its own 2025 state, so the re-based SSP2 and the
original SSP2 describe the same trajectory. All five scenarios share an identical 2025
population of approximately 8.15 billion, and divergence between them emerges only after
2025. The SSP2 file therefore serves as the reference pathway for the set.

Scenario assumptions. Fertility and educational-attainment transitions follow the
SSP-specific assumptions of the corresponding WIC2023 pathway. Mortality follows the
low-mortality variant under SSP1 and SSP5 and the high-mortality variant under SSP3,
consistent with the SSP narratives (O'Neill et al., 2017). SSP4 combines the two by country
group: high-fertility countries take the high-mortality schedule, as in SSP3, while the
remaining countries follow the medium schedule used for SSP2. Migration is modelled with
age-specific emigration and immigration rates, with net international migration converging
to zero by 2060 and an additional correction applied to migration below age 15. All
scenarios carry the Ukraine displacement adjustment used in the WIC2023 baseline.

Outputs. Each file reports population stocks by cell together with the period flows that
generate them, births, deaths, immigration, and emigration, for every five-year period
from 2025 to 2100.

Status. These are scenario outputs, not probabilistic forecasts. They make a set of
internally consistent assumptions explicit and traceable; they are not predictions, and
long-run country-level results for small territories should be interpreted with care.

metadata.title: Comparative profitability analysis of land uses between Eucalyptus woodlot and crop production: evidence from Dangila Woreda, Northwest Ethiopia
metadata.description: This study assessed the financial profitability of two land use systems (Eucalyptus versus crop production) in Dangila Woreda, where there is a significant shift toward Eucalyptus woodlots. The expansion of Eucalyptus on arable land competes with food crop production and threatens household food security in the study area. Previously, land use allocation was not based on systematic feasibility assessments. This study evaluated the profitability of the two land uses using financial indicators (NPV and BCR). A multi-stage sampling technique was used to select 316 respondents from four randomly selected kebeles. To evaluate financial profitability, both primary and secondary data were used, including focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and household surveys. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-square tests, trend analysis, and NPV and BCR analyses. The results showed that Eucalyptus woodlot plantations have increased in area over time. The profitability analysis indicated that the Eucalyptus investment generates a significantly higher NPV of 193,978.66 ETB/ha and a BCR of 4.69, whereas crop production yields an NPV of 162,699.13 ETB/ha and a BCR of 1.32. Across sensitivity analysis scenarios, Eucalyptus plantations consistently provide higher net returns and a more favorable return on investment. Despite its higher return, the Eucalyptus planting site must be identified and chosen in consultation with experts to minimize competition with food production.

metadata.title: Sovereign Green Bonds and India's Climate Finance Strategy: An Empirical Assessment of Pricing, Demand, and Comparative Positioning
metadata.description: India's Sovereign Green Bond (SGrB) programme, launched in January 2023, was designed to serve three purposes at once: to lower the government's own cost of borrowing through a pricing discount known as the greenium, to widen the base of climate-conscious investors, and to signal institutional credibility on climate commitments to international markets. This paper offers an empirical, data-grounded assessment of how far the programme has achieved these aims over its first three years of operation, drawing on Reserve Bank of India auction records, market commentary, and a comparative review of four other emerging-market sovereign issuers: Chile, Indonesia, Nigeria, and Poland. The analysis finds that India's greenium has been inconsistent rather than dependable: an early positive differential gave way to a confirmed negative greenium of 9 basis points at the August 2024 auction, meaning the government paid a premium rather than a discount to issue green. Investor demand, measured through subscription ratios, has also weakened over time, from 4.11 times the notified amount at the debut auction to close to parity by mid-2024. Placed alongside Chile, Indonesia, and Nigeria, India's cumulative issuance covers under 1 per cent of its own annual climate finance requirement, a smaller share than Chile's, though larger than Nigeria's. The paper concludes that SGrBs have, so far, functioned more effectively as an instrument of institutional signalling and market development than as a reliable source of cost savings, and it sets out specific, data-supported recommendations for improving reporting transparency, deepening the domestic investor base, and scaling issuance.
keywords: Sovereign Green Bonds, Greenium, Climate Finance, India, Reserve Bank of India, Comparative Analysis, Sustainable Finance

dates.description: Climate change has moved from being treated as a peripheral environmental concern to a central fiscal and macroeconomic one, particularly for large developing economies such as India. India has committed to reducing the emission intensity of its GDP by 45 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030 and to reaching net-zero emissions by 2070 (Government of India, 2022). Meeting these commitments requires climate finance on a scale that dwarfs current flows: estimates of the cumulative requirement by 2030 range up to ₹217.5 lakh crore, rising to ₹878.7 lakh crore by 2070 (Deloitte, 2025; Climate Risk Horizons, 2026).

metadata.title: QSM-CI method: SUSEP-Net (v2)
metadata.description:
SUSEP-Net — a simulation-supervised, contrastive-learning deep network for sub-voxel susceptibility source separation. A dual-branch 3D U-net with two guidance encoders maps the R2′, local field and χ_total (QSM) images to the paramagnetic (χ+, iron) and diamagnetic (χ−, myelin·calcium) source maps. Run here via PyTorch on CPU, whole-volume, z-scored inputs (QSM/field in ppm, R2′ in Hz).

QSM-CI reconstruction method susep-net. Browse and run it at https://qsmxt.github.io/QSM-CI/submission.html?method=susep-net.

RESUMEN
La comunicación pública de la ciencia en arqueología ha experimentado una expansión a partir del uso de entornos digitales, favoreciendo el diálogo entre la producción científica y diversos públicos. Este trabajo analiza la experiencia del proyecto Tecnoriginaria: Saberes de los Pueblos Originarios, dirigido a estudiantes de nivel primario (8 a 13 años). El objetivo consistió en la producción de microvideos para redes sociales con el fin de comunicar aspectos del pasado prehispánico del Noroeste Argentino, las prácticas y metodologías del quehacer arqueológico. Desde un enfoque interdisciplinario, se implementó una estrategia transmedia basada en la construcción de narrativas distribuidas en múltiples plataformas digitales. La propuesta incorporó personajes como recurso de mediación para facilitar la apropiación del conocimiento. Los resultados evidencian una recepción positiva y un marcado interés por contenidos vinculados con tecnologías prehispánicas. Las métricas de redes sociales indican un alcance significativo hacia audiencias no seguidoras, con dificultades en la consolidación de una comunidad estable. Se concluye que el uso de narrativas digitales breves y personajes constituye una estrategia eficaz, una herramienta necesaria para fortalecer el rol social de las ciencias, visibilizar y explicitar los compromisos asumidos con la sociedad y promover procesos de apropiación del conocimiento amplios, inclusivos y participativos.

ABSTRACT
The public communication of science in archaeology has undergone a significant expansion through the use of digital environments, fostering dialogue between scientific production and diverse audiences. This paper analyzes the experience of the project "Tecnoriginaria: Saberes de los Pueblos Originarios," aimed at primary school students (aged 8 to 13). The objective consisted of producing micro-videos for social media to communicate aspects of the pre-Hispanic past of Northwest Argentina, as well as the practices and methodologies of archaeological work. Adopting an interdisciplinary approach, a transmedia strategy was implemented based on the construction of narratives distributed across multiple digital platforms. The proposal incorporated characters as a mediation resource to facilitate the appropriation of knowledge. The results demonstrate a positive reception and a marked interest in content related to pre-Hispanic technologies. Social media metrics indicate a significant reach toward non-follower audiences, although difficulties were observed in consolidating a stable community. The study concludes that the use of brief digital narratives and characters constitutes an effective strategy, a necessary tool to strengthen the social role of the sciences, to make explicit the commitments made to society, and to promote broader, more inclusive, and participatory processes of knowledge appropriation.

metadata.title: PROMICE | GC-NET automatic weather station data
metadata.description:
The article documents the integration and enhancement of meteorological and glaciological observations from 52 active and historical automatic weather station (AWS) sites across the Greenland Ice Sheet and surrounding areas. It outlines recent hardware improvements in station design and sensor configurations tailored for both accumulation and ablation zones. Additionally, the paper details the standardized, reproducible data processing workflow—implemented via the open-source pypromice Python package—used for calibration, filtering, and variable derivation to support research in polar meteorology, climatology, and glaciology.

Parts of the data treatment routines presented here were supported by the European Union's Horizon Europe programme through the project LIQUIDICE (grant no. 101184962).

metadata.description: The textbook provides a systematic framework for the classification, evolution, and practical application of wired and wireless interfaces in microcontroller systems and the Internet of Things. Physical, electrical, logical, and software interface layers; on-chip buses; wired serial protocols; wireless technologies; and application protocols are examined. Special attention is paid to criteria for selecting the optimal interface, multi-layer security, and practical case studies. For students, graduate students, and engineers in the fields of computer engineering, automation, and information technology.
